documents.title: WHO Guidelines for the Management of Snakebites
documents.content: Immobilize the affected limb using a broad bandage or splint. Keep the patient completely still and calm to slow venom circulation. Transport immediately to a healthcare facility equipped with antivenom. Never cut the bite wound, suction venom, apply arterial tourniquets, ice, or herbal home remedies. Venomous snakebites from cobras, vipers, or kraits require rapid hospital evaluation.
immediateActions: Call emergency services (112 / 108) or arrange immediate transport to a hospital with antivenom.
Keep the patient completely still, calm, and immobile to slow venom spreading.
Immobilize the bitten limb with a splint or loose sling at or slightly below heart level.
Remove rings, watches, shoes, and tight clothing before swelling starts.
doNotDo: DO NOT cut, incise, or slash the bite wound.
DO NOT attempt suction by mouth, pump, or vacuum device.
DO NOT apply tight arterial tourniquets or tight bands.
DO NOT apply ice, cold packs, or electric shocks.
DO NOT give herbal remedies, alcohol, or unverified home treatments.
warningSigns: Difficulty breathing or swallowing
Drooping eyelids or blurred vision
Rapid swelling or severe localized pain
Spontaneous bleeding from gums or nose

documents.source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India
documents.title: Standard Treatment Guidelines for Snakebite in India
documents.content: Reassure the victim. Immobilize the bitten limb at or slightly below heart level. Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing before swelling develops. Immediately transport the patient to the nearest hospital capable of providing anti-snake venom (ASV). Strictly avoid traditional healers, tourniquets, cutting, or sucking.
immediateActions: Reassure victim and maintain strict physical immobility.
Remove all restrictive jewelry, rings, and tight footwear immediately.
Immobilize limb using rigid splint or sling.
Transport directly to nearest facility providing Anti-Snake Venom (ASV).
doNotDo: DO NOT apply tight tourniquets or tight strings.
DO NOT cut wound or attempt suction.
DO NOT visit traditional healers or delay hospital transfer.
warningSigns: Ptosis (drooping eyelids)
Difficulty speaking or swallowing
Dark colored urine or non-clotting blood

documents.source: WHO & International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
documents.title: Basic Emergency Care (BEC): Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
documents.content: If conscious and unable to cough or breathe, deliver 5 sharp back blows between shoulder blades followed by 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver). If patient becomes unconscious, lower to ground and begin CPR immediately while checking airway.
immediateActions: Encourage patient to cough forcefully if capable of coughing.
If unable to speak or breathe, lean patient forward and deliver 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades.
Perform 5 quick inward and upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) just above the navel.
If victim collapses unconscious, lower carefully to floor and begin chest compressions CPR.
doNotDo: DO NOT perform blind finger sweeps in the mouth.
DO NOT slap back while patient is standing upright without forward lean.
warningSigns: Inability to talk or cry out
Clutching throat with hands (universal choking sign)
Turning blue or pale cyanosis

documents.title: WHO Emergency Care Toolkit - Burn First Aid
documents.content: Cool the burn immediately under cool running tap water for 10-20 minutes. Remove non-adherent clothing and jewelry before swelling occurs. Cover loosely with sterile non-stick bandage or clean cling wrap. Do not apply ice, toothpaste, butter, or unverified ointments.
immediateActions: Cool burn immediately with cool running water for 10 to 20 minutes.
Gently remove clothing and rings around burn before swelling starts.
Cover clean wound loosely with sterile non-stick dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Keep patient warm with blanket over uninjured areas to prevent hypothermia.
doNotDo: DO NOT apply ice, ice water, or freezing substances directly to skin.
DO NOT apply toothpaste, butter, oil, grease, or traditional ointments.
DO NOT pop or burst blisters.
DO NOT peel off clothing stuck tightly to burned skin.
warningSigns: Burns covering face, hands, feet, groin, or major joints
Charred, leathery black or white skin
Inhalation injury indicated by coughing or soot around mouth/nose

documents.title: WHO-ICRC Basic Emergency Care - Hemorrhage Control
documents.content: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure over the bleeding wound using a clean cloth or sterile dressing. Elevate injured area if possible. Maintain pressure without removing initial dressing. Call emergency services immediately for severe arterial bleeding.
immediateActions: Apply immediate direct firm manual pressure directly over wound using sterile gauze or clean cloth.
Maintain uninterrupted pressure for at least 10 minutes.
Add additional cloth pads over initial layer if blood soaks through.
Have patient lie down flat and elevate injured bleeding limb above heart if possible.
doNotDo: DO NOT remove original pressure pad if blood soaks through; add more layers on top.
DO NOT loosen direct pressure to check wound repeatedly.
DO NOT apply improvised tourniquets unless trained for catastrophic extremity arterial hemorrhage.
warningSigns: Pulsatile spurting bright red arterial blood
Signs of hemorrhagic shock (pale, cold clammy skin, confusion, rapid weak pulse)

documents.title: WHO Guidelines for Poisoning Management & Toxic Ingestion
documents.content: In cases of chemical or toxic ingestion, do not induce vomiting. Bring the chemical container or label to emergency department. If chemical is on skin or eyes, flush immediately with clean water for 15-20 minutes. Keep victim sitting up if conscious.
immediateActions: Call emergency services (112 / 108) or poison control center immediately.
Identify substance, bottle, label, or chemical container and bring it to hospital.
If chemical splashed in eye or skin, flush continuous clean water for 15 to 20 minutes.
If conscious, place patient in comfortable sitting position to protect airway.
doNotDo: DO NOT induce vomiting unless explicitly instructed by medical professional.
DO NOT give salt water, raw eggs, milk, or vinegar.
DO NOT attempt neutralizations with acids or alkalis.
warningSigns: Drowsiness, confusion, or loss of consciousness
Difficulty breathing or abnormal heart rhythm
Chemical burns around lips or inside mouth

documents.title: WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) - Seizure Protocol
documents.content: Protect person from injury by moving nearby hard objects. Place soft padding under head. Turn person onto side in recovery position to prevent aspiration. Do not insert anything into mouth or restrain movements.
immediateActions: Ease person to floor and clear surrounding area of hard, sharp objects.
Place soft folded jacket or pillow under patient head.
Turn person gently onto side (recovery position) to keep airway clear of saliva or vomit.
Time the duration of the seizure episode accurately.
doNotDo: DO NOT force any object, spoon, finger, or cloth into mouth.
DO NOT forcibly hold down or restrain seizing movements.
DO NOT offer food, liquid, or oral medicine until fully awake.
warningSigns: Seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes
Second seizure starts immediately after first without regaining consciousness
Patient is pregnant, diabetic, or suffered head trauma

documents.source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) & WHO
documents.title: Clinical Protocol for Acute Ischemic Stroke Management
documents.content: Identify FAST signs: Facial drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency 112 immediately. Note exact time symptoms started. Keep patient lying down with shoulders slightly elevated.
immediateActions: Perform FAST test: Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency.
Call 112 / 108 immediately; acute stroke treatment is time-critical (thrombolysis window).
Note exact timestamp when symptoms first appeared.
Keep patient resting comfortably lying flat or with head elevated 30 degrees.
doNotDo: DO NOT give aspirin, food, water, or oral medications before hospital CT scan.
DO NOT allow patient to sleep or delay transport.
warningSigns: Sudden numbness or paralysis on one side of body
Sudden loss of vision, speech, or balance

documents.source: World Health Organization (WHO) & International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation
documents.title: WHO Basic Life Support & CPR Protocol
documents.content: For severe crushing chest pain, tightness, or pressure radiating to arm, neck, or jaw: call emergency services 112 immediately. Keep patient sitting upright comfortably. If patient becomes unresponsive and stops breathing, initiate hands-only CPR chest compressions immediately at 100-120 compressions per minute.
immediateActions: Call emergency services (112 / 108) immediately for acute chest pain.
Have patient sit comfortably upright, rest physically, and stop all exertion.
Loosen collar, belt, and tight clothing.
If victim collapses, loses pulse, and stops breathing, begin CPR chest compressions over center of chest (100-120 BPM).
doNotDo: DO NOT leave patient unattended.
DO NOT allow patient to walk, exert, or drive to hospital.
warningSigns: Crushing central chest tightness radiating to left arm, back, or jaw
Profuse cold sweating, nausea, dizziness, or shortness of breath
